recipes.name: Mushroom Sauce Baked Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 2-quart baking dish with 1 tablespoon butter and set aside.
Rub pork chops with salt, garlic powder, and pepper. Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook chops in hot butter until brown on both sides. Remove chops to a plate.
Cook and stir onions in drippings in the same skillet until browned. Pour in condensed soup and milk; stir until blended. Remove from heat and set aside.
Arrange potatoes evenly in the prepared baking dish. Place chops on top of potatoes. Pour soup mixture over chops.

Bake, covered, in the preheated oven for 30 minutes. Uncover and continue baking until potatoes are tender and chops are cooked through, about 30 minutes more. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of a chop should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Mushroom Sauce Baked Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: These oven-baked pork chops with cream of mushroom soup and sliced potatoes in a creamy onion sauce are a simple family-favorite weeknight dinner.

video.description: Nothing quite as delicious as potatoes and pork chops! An easy meal to prepare for a delicious outcome! Layer the dish with butter, thinly sliced potatoes then add pork chops and mushroom sauce on top and bake!

review.reviewBody: This is a nice "homey" recipe (even myself and my bf - both of us confirmed mushroom haters!) liked this! I like the fact that it is a meal-in-one dish. Be sure to slice your potatoes thin so that they cook all the way through in the alloted amount of time called for, or else your pork chops will be overdone and your potatoes won't be completely cooked. I seasoned my chops with seasoned salt in lieu of table salt to add more flavor (I didn't pre measure the salt, pepper or garlic powder either - just seasoned to taste). I also added some minced garlic from a jar to the soup mixture and shredded cheddar cheese to cover the casserole. This is similar to the pork chop and potato casserole recipe by Wendy on this site (hence the idea for adding cheese). The pork chops go well with green beans or a tossed salad and dinner rolls on the side. A cold glass of milk completes the meal! This one's a definite keeper : ) Thanks!

I made this almost exactly as written. I did add 4 cloves of minced fresh garlic and about 1/2 teaspoon of thyme. I used thin pork chops which made it pretty simple to make. Next time, I would a couple more potatoes. I thin sliced the potatoes and only used a layer of them because I was afraid of them not cooking through. I was very glad I checked the potatoes after 45 minutes because they were done. This is a pretty simple recipe that could be dressed up with a some fresh chopped parsley and a little white or red wine to deglaze the pan once the chops are browned. Also, I used 3 quart Pyrex for this.

I used an oven-safe skillet for the pork and then onions with mushrooms. Mixed the soup with 1 cup milk and added it on top. Baked in covered skillet for 45 minutes and everything turned out perfect. No potatoes.

I give this recipe four stars because my husband loves it and because it requires so much tweeking to make it really good.
 I'm glad that I read the reviews before preparation. Doing so saved me a lot of frustration. I added an extra can of soup, used chicken broth instead of milk, added four buds (finely chopped) of garlic, one tbs. ground garlic, two tsp. basil, 1/2 tsp. lemon pepper, two bay leafs, some red pepper flakes, one tsp. parsley, and a half cup of white wine. Because others had difficulty with the potatoes, I sliced mine ultra thin and microwaved them for six minutes thinking that might improve the cooking time. It still took them an hour and a half to bake. 
I will make this again because hubby likes it so much. Next time, I think I will take the advice of another reviewer and rub the chops with onion soup to enrich the flavor. I think I might just pre-boil the potatoes to al dente in chicken broth to significantly improve their flavor and to cut way down on bake time. I think the dish would only need to bake for about thirty five minutes if I do that. This is a good basic recipe. There are so many things you could do to improve or to just change the flavor. I think it would be good with chicken soup and curry also. If I find any really good improvements I'll post them.

Great sauce. I started by sautéing some onions, then added the protein (chicken) along with three Rosemary sprigs, and cooked for about 5 minutes on each side. I removed that to a baking dish, then deglazed the pan with a little white wine, to which I added garlic and mushrooms. I cooked that for a couple of minutes then added the milk and soup. I poured the mixture over the meat and baked for about 45 minutes. We really enjoyed it. Thanks for sharing

Extremely easy to make, this is a definite comfort food. I made mine to the recipe except used one onion only , keeping in mind to slice the potatoes VERY thin. (thanks,all, for the advice; it was spot on! An hour in the oven sufficed.) DH enjoyed it, tho' he's not an onion fan. My biggest problem was what to serve with it to contrast the creamy richness of the sauce. I decided on a salad with vinaigrette dressing. Next time I will make it using one potato per serving, (4 cups sliced potatoes = 2 raw potatoes) and might de-glaze the pan with a little white wine like somebody suggested. If I make this for my DIL, I will put some hot sauce on the table for her.

Delightfully tender pork chops -- probably the most moist I've made in a long time. For thin chops, I cut the time to 30 covered and 15 uncovered, with no potatoes. I also added a handful of sliced, sauteed cremini mushrooms.

I made half the recipe, kept the full can of soup, sliced the potatoes thinly, and added fresh chopped mushrooms. Prepared it early, kept it refrigerated, then baked it later in the day. Came out great.

I made this for dinner for friends and everyone loved it even mushroom haters!! I did tweek the recipe a bit to make it even better I cooked it in a cast iron pot with the lid on for 2 hours stirring every 30 mins it made the pork fall apart and was so Delish! I also did fresh garlic instead of garlic powder and I sautéed some diced mushroom and seasoning blend (unions, &bell peppers) and added that to the mix and made mashed potatoes and poured the mushroom pork sauce on top It was so delicious!!

My family all loved it. I too added mushrooms and garlic to it, and used 2 golden mushroom soup for color and one can cream of mushroom( I was cooking 9 pork chops). I heard from reviews that it was on the salty side so I didn't add any salt, but it still was too salty for me. I also precooked the sliced potatoes in the oven, but this ended up being unnecessary, and they ended up all mushy. Oh well,lesson learned. The family still liked it. Oh and I added shredded Monterey cheddar cheese at the end and let that melt all over the top, the family really seemed to like that! I'll make again but prolly try and find a way to cut through all the salt! I'm assuming it's from the soup and garlic, so instead of one of the cans, I'll add sour cream. Thanks for the recipe!

I used cream of chicken and I cut the chops into 1 1/2 in cubes for easy of eating
I also added 1/4 cup choppedJalapeno along with everything else..
I added 1 cup mozzerela cheese on top 10 min before done....
It was plain SLAMMIN !!

great recipe, I added worshishire sauce to the soup and milk mixture, added parsley as well and layered the pototos and onions on the bottom with chops on top; sprinkled a little cheese on before serving.
The ONLY change I made was to add some chopped fresh mushrooms with the onions. Great re pie.
I used white rice instead of potatoes . Turned out great !
good but is missing a bit more flavor. I will try making it again
Wonderful flavour, easy to make, only thing I added was some dried red bell peppers. We all loved this recipe and will make it again and again.
10/10, especially after adding numerous tips from the reviews. Definitely my go to recipe for pork chops!
Zero flavor. Will not make again

I buy the large packages of pork chops when they go on sale then divide into two chops for a quick inexpensive dinner that hits the mark on a cold winter night. I love coarse pepper and heavy cream in this.
Sooo Good! And easy to make. Family Favorite. Thank you!
